message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total — within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with no funds transferred out of the account). The case for buying: Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue came in at $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 net sales were $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS, and operating income of $123.2B — a highly profitable franchise with modest but positive growth, and the FY net income dip was driven by a one-time $10.2B tax charge rather than operating deterioration. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were trading around $222 with analysts focused on iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which I treated as a reasonable entry point rather than a reason to wait. I sized the position modestly (about 20% of available cash) given the mixed signals on iPhone demand and the fact that I already hold MSFT, keeping the limit price essentially at the current market ($222.68 bid / $222.72 ask) so the order was executable rather than a speculative lowball.
